text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas backed off on Wednesday from his suggestion to establish unilaterally the sea border between Latvia and Lithuania and said that all previous agreements between the two countries were null and void.
- A total of 10 AK-47 machine guns were stolen from the defence ministry arsenal in Radviliskis.

- The coalition of the Homeland Union and Christian Democrats started talks on a new cabinet of ministers. The party is to nominate the chairman of parliament and new prime minister while the Christian Democrats will take responsibility for foreign affairs, defence and a third ministry, yet to be decided. Both parties also decided to reduce the number of ministries by three to 16.
- Mazheikiu Nafta has bought and refined 50,000 tonnes of crude oil acquired using a credit from U.S. securities house Merrill Lynch.
- President Brazauskas renounced earlier agreements with Latvia.

- Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele claims that he sees no big problems in establishing a Lithuanian/Latvian sea boarder. He says he intends to solve the existing problems in the next three to 10 months after the new Lithuanian government has been formed.
- During the first 10 months of this year the state budget collected 3.8 billion litas out of a planned 4.9 billion litas, the state tax inspection said.

- An advisor to Brazauskas said the president would start consulatations over his nomination for prime minister after the official election results have been announced on November 15. He said talks would start on November 20 and continue until December 5.
- The defeated Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP), routed by the right-wing in the elections, said that other parties were "burying us too early".
